items.stem: A prompt places a long, unchanging instruction block AFTER the user's changing question. Why does this undermine prompt caching?

options.text: Caching reuses a stable prefix; putting changing content first prevents the stable block from being cached
options.rationale: Correct: a reusable prefix must come before variable content.

options.text: Caching only works on output tokens
options.rationale: Caching concerns the input prefix, not output.

options.text: Instruction blocks can never be cached
options.rationale: Stable instruction blocks are exactly what caching targets.
Ordering is a design choice, not a restriction.

items.explanation: Correct: a reusable prefix must come before variable content.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO actions genuinely reduce token cost? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Trim irrelevant context that the task does not need
options.rationale: Correct: fewer input tokens cost less.

options.text: Constrain the output length when a short answer suffices
options.rationale: Correct: shorter outputs reduce output-token cost.

options.text: Add filler context to 'help' the model
options.rationale: Filler inflates token count and cost.
Larger models can cost more without improving a simple task.

items.explanation: Correct: fewer input tokens cost less.

items.stem: Before claiming a caching change saved money, what should you do?

options.text: Measure actual cache hits and cost in usage metrics
options.rationale: Correct: verify real behaviour rather than trusting a projection.

options.text: Assume the saving because the prompt looks shorter
Switch off monitoring to reduce overhead
options.rationale: Monitoring is how you verify the saving.
Logs are needed to confirm the effect.

items.explanation: Correct: verify real behaviour rather than trusting a projection.
